# `js/import-no-rename-default`

**A default import should go by the default export's own name**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-js` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-js` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX |
| **Turned on by** | no preset — name it in `[rules]` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | none — severity only |
| **Fix** | `manual` — no automatic fix; the steps are under *How to fix* (the right name is the one the default export has in its own file; renaming a binding is left to the author because other names in the importing file may already use it) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.5.0 |
| **Scope** | project — reads the whole repository through the project graph, not one file at a time |
| **Ported from** | `eslint-plugin-import-x/no-rename-default` |

## What it checks

A default import (`import x from "./m"`, or `import { default as x } from "./m"`) bound to a name other than the one the default export has in `./m` is reported. That name is the function or class declared (`export default function make() {}`), the identifier exported (`export default widget`), the first argument of the call it wraps (`export default connect(Panel)` is `Panel`), or the local of `export { item as default }`. An anonymous default export, a default that is re-exported from elsewhere, and a module that is not an ES module have no name to compare. Upstream's `commonjs` and `preventRenamingBindings` options are not built; the rule reads as upstream's defaults, except that `require()` is not checked.

**Why:** a default export has no name at the import, so the name each importer picks is the only name the thing has; one module imported under three names is three names to search for.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-js
pip install codelaw-rules-js
```

**No preset turns it on.** Load its pack through any preset (`codelaw:js/recommended` here), then name the rule in `[rules]`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:js/recommended"]

[rules]
"js/import-no-rename-default" = "error"
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"js/import-no-rename-default" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — the `tests` scope `codelaw:js/recommended` ships (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`); naming it extends it, so its files stay:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/import-no-rename-default" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"js/import-no-rename-default" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"js/import-no-rename-default" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"js/import-no-rename-default" = { severity = "warn" }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "js/import-no-rename-default": {"severity": "warn"}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore js/import-no-rename-default: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore js/import-no-rename-default expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule js/import-no-rename-default --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain js/import-no-rename-default       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule js/import-no-rename-default  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>               # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Rename the binding to the name the message gives, and every use of it.
2. Or rename the default export to the name the importers use, in its own file.

## Examples

### JavaScript

#### Don't

```js files
// src/make.js
export default function makeWidget() {}
// src/app.js
import build from "./make";
console.log(build());
```

#### Do

```js files
// src/make.js
export default function makeWidget() {}
// src/app.js
import makeWidget from "./make";
console.log(makeWidget());
```

### JSX

#### Don't

```jsx files
// src/make.jsx
export default function makeWidget() {}
// src/app.jsx
import build from "./make";
console.log(build());
```

#### Do

```jsx files
// src/make.jsx
export default function makeWidget() {}
// src/app.jsx
import makeWidget from "./make";
console.log(makeWidget());
```

### TypeScript

#### Don't

```ts files
// src/make.ts
export default function makeWidget() {}
// src/app.ts
import build from "./make";
console.log(build());
```

#### Do

```ts files
// src/make.ts
export default function makeWidget() {}
// src/app.ts
import makeWidget from "./make";
console.log(makeWidget());
```

### TSX

#### Don't

```tsx files
// src/make.tsx
export default function makeWidget() {}
// src/app.tsx
import build from "./make";
console.log(build());
```

#### Do

```tsx files
// src/make.tsx
export default function makeWidget() {}
// src/app.tsx
import makeWidget from "./make";
console.log(makeWidget());
```
